forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Stratford-on-Avon: Housing Benefits £170,815 over budget at Period 6, £50,000 over forecast for 2026/27
news_drafts.lead:
Stratford-on-Avon's Cabinet, meeting on 2 November 2026, has budget monitoring papers (the in-year check of spending against budget) showing Housing Benefits £170,815 over budget at Period 6. The estimated outturn (the actual figure once the year has ended) for 2026/27 is an overspend of £50,000. The report attributes the Period 6 variance to under-recovery of housing benefit overpayments and a shortfall in housing benefit subsidy. The line carries an expenditure budget of £8.4m to Period 6.

Property, which sits under the Environmental and Neighbourhood Services directorate, has an expenditure budget of £326,415 to Period 6 and an overall variance of £132,311. Its estimated outturn for 2026/27 is a £200,000 overspend, the largest adverse outturn in that directorate.

The council's risk register also covers HEART, the home adaptations service. It says the budget "follows a period of poor performance and underspending, followed by a period where the budget is overspent by mid year", and that a service improvement plan has "delivered a significant change in the outturn of the team". Works have been stockpiled for 2026/27, which the register says creates a risk of budget pressures early in that year. The council will work with HEART on whether to allocate further in-year funding above planned commitments. Nuneaton & Bedworth Borough Council has given notice to cease the existing service on 31 March 2027, and an options review is listed for winter 2026.

findings.headline: The Gaydon/Lighthorne Heath affordable housing S106 balance of £1,467,129.09 is recorded with its second tranche unpaid
findings.detail: The Taylor Wimpey Midlands affordable housing balance at Gaydon/Lighthorne Heath is shown as uncommitted, with a note that two tranches are unpaid. The paper gives the final instalment as due after the unpaid tranche plus ten years.
findings.matters: A large affordable housing balance with an unpaid tranche shows that part of the expected funding has not yet arrived, which affects how much the council can plan to spend.

findings.headline: Several S106 balances carry spend-by dates before 30/09/2026, including £27,607.26 for Campden Road public open space with a Sep-26 date
findings.detail: The uncommitted Taylor Wimpey Midlands line for Shipston-on-Stour youth and adult amenity has a Sep-26 spend-by date, and a Damson Homes line has a Dec-25 date. Committed balances at Gaydon (Mar-26) and McCarthy Stone (Jan-24) also show dates that have passed.
findings.matters: Balances still held past their spend-by dates raise a question about whether the council can spend or must return the money, which other councils face on the same agreements.

findings.headline: A Housestyle Countrywide affordable housing S106 balance of £26,794.93 is shown as unpaid since 30/09/24 and cannot be committed
findings.detail: The paper records the balance as an unpaid invoice that the council cannot count as committed. A second Housestyle balance on the same planning reference is shown as committed, and its invoice status is not stated.
findings.matters: Developer contributions that are invoiced but unpaid for years are money a council may not collect, so peers reviewing their own S106 receivables would want the age of this debt.

findings.headline: The Crossroads Alcester Academy's CIL allocation of £85,403.01 is recorded as refunded by the grantee for a project underspend
findings.detail: The paid-out CIL IFS line shows £85,403.01 with the note that the grantee refunded the project underspend. The refund is recorded within the 2025-26 paid-out total of £292,651.01.
findings.matters: Grant-funded projects that return unspent money are a recovery route that other councils running similar CIL funding programmes would want to see recorded.
findings.figures: £85,403.01 refunded underspend; £292,651.01 total CIL IFS spend 2025-26

findings.headline: A £282,000.00 CIL allocation for the Alcester Road cycle route, recorded under Cabinet Minute 555, is still shown as committed at 30/09/2026
findings.detail: The allocation is listed as CIL IFS 21/22 with no spend-by date, and the minute is dated 06/02/23. It remains in the committed CIL contributions at the 30/09/2026 balance date.
findings.matters: An allocation more than three years old that is still open shows how long CIL allocations can stay committed without a recorded spend date.
findings.figures: £282,000.00 allocated; Cabinet Minute 555 dated 06/02/23; total committed CIL £1,806,500.00
